{{Tooltip|W|Won}} 82–76 vs. [[2012–13 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]] (vacated) }} {{2012–13 Big East men's basketball standings}} The '''2012–13 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Louisville]] during the [[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]], Louisville's 99th season of intercollegiate competition. The Cardinals competed in the [[Big East Conference (1979–2013)|Big East Conference]] and were coached by [[Rick Pitino]] in his 12th season as head coach at Louisville. The team played its home games on [[Denny Crum]] Court at the [[KFC Yum! Center]]. The Cardinals finished the season 35–5, 14–4 in Big East play to earn a share of the Big East regular season championship. They won the Big East tournament for the third time in school history and received the conference's automatic bid to the NCAA tournament. The Cardinals earned a trip to the school's tenth Final Four and defeated [[2012–13 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]] to win the NCAA Championship. Siva was named to the All-Big East Third Team. ==Postseason== ===Big East tournament=== The Cardinals were the number 2 seed in the tournament and faced [[Villanova Men's Basketball Team|Villanova]] in the quarter-finals, defeating them, 74–55.{{cite news|title=Russ Smith leads Louisville over Villanova, into Big East semifinals|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330730097|agency=Associated Press|access-date=June 1, 2013|archive-date=May 20, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130520155304/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=330730097|url-status=live}} They next defeated [[2012–13 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team|number 24 Notre Dame]], 69–57,{{cite news|title=Louisville downs Irish in Big East semifinals for third straight year|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330740097|agency=Associated Press|access-date=June 1, 2013|archive-date=May 9, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130509050246/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=330740097|url-status=live}} setting up the final Big East tournament championship game against [[2012–13 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|number 19 Syracuse]]. Louisville was down by 16 in the second half, but rallied to claim their third Big East tournament championship with a 78–61 victory. The Cardinals repeated as tournament champions.{{cite news|title=Louisville rallies from 16 down to win 2nd straight Big East title|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330750097|agency=Associated Press|access-date=June 1, 2013|archive-date=May 17, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130517111656/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=330750097|url-status=live}} ===NCAA tournament=== Louisville received the number 1 overall seed in the Midwest Region of the [[2013 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament.]]{{cite news|title=Louisville claims top overall seed|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/9063277/2013-ncaa-tournament-louisville-cardinals-named-top-overall-seed|agency=Associated Press|access-date=June 1, 2013|archive-date=June 5, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130605015547/http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/9063277/2013-ncaa-tournament-louisville-cardinals-named-top-overall-seed|url-status=live}} They opened the tournament with a 79–48 win over [[North Carolina A&T Aggies men's basketball|North Carolina A&T]], setting the NCAA tournament single-game record for steals with 20. They closed out the opening weekend by defeating [[2012–13 Colorado State Rams men's basketball team|Colorado State]], 82–56. They defeated [[2012–13 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team|Oregon]] in the regional semi-final, 77–69, to set up a regional final with [[2012–13 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]], whom they had lost to in the season-opening tournament. Before halftime of the game Louisville guard [[Kevin Ware]] suffered a compound fracture. The Cardinals rallied together to defeat Duke by 22 (the largest tournament defeat for coach [[Mike Krzyzewski]] since the 1990 National Title Game), 85–63. The Cardinals advanced to their second consecutive Final Four (their 10th) to face [[2012–13 Wichita State Shockers men's basketball team|Wichita State]]. The Shockers led most of the game, and were up by as many as 12 with 13 minutes to play. A 20-point performance by [[Luke Hancock]], and two timely three-point shots by walk-on Tim Henderson, kept the Cardinals in the game, which they won, 72–68, to advance to face [[2012–13 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]] in the National Championship. In its third NCAA Championship game Louisville went down 12 points. The Cardinals rallied behind a 22-point effort by Final Four MOP Luke Hancock, 18 points and 5 assists from senior captain Peyton Siva, and 15 points and 12 rebounds from sophomore [[Chane Behanan]] to win, 82–76, giving Louisville basketball its third NCAA Championship and giving coach Rick Pitino his first title at Louisville. ==Schedule and results== {{CBB schedule start|gamehighs=yes|attend=yes}} |- !colspan=12 style="background:#AD0000; color:#FFFFFF;"|Exhibition {{CBB schedule entry | date = November 1, 2012 | time = 7:00 pm | nonconf = yes | homecoming = | away = | neutral = | rank = 2 | opponent = [[University of Pikeville|Pikeville]] | opprank = | site_stadium = [[KFC Yum!
